sources.text: Founder note: Amani Cycle Repair plans a mobile bicycle repair service in Cape Town, initially serving commuter hubs and university residences.

Interview summary: 12 informal conversations were reported; four people said they had paid for bicycle repairs in the past year. No recordings, survey method, or signed pilot commitments were supplied.
Draft price sheet: call-out fee ZAR 120 plus parts; founder estimates average parts cost ZAR 180 and 45 minutes per repair. No invoices, competitor price checks, or time logs are attached.
Founder states one mechanic and one borrowed van are available on weekends; no vehicle agreement, insurance record, or service-area capacity plan was supplied.
No registered entity documents, dated customer evidence, pilot bookings, verified cost ledger, or operating permission for the proposed service locations were attached.
